title: Python for Data Science: Environment & Libraries
description: Mixed-format quiz (MCQ, true/false, select-all) on Anaconda, Jupyter Notebooks, functions, dictionaries in data handling, and the core Data Science/ML libraries (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch) — aligned with the university question bank (Q6, Q8–Q10).

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason Python is preferred for Data Science?
options: Its syntax reads almost like plain English, lowering the barrier to entry for non-professional programmers
It is a compiled language requiring manual memory management
It has no ready-made libraries for numerical computing
It cannot be used for data visualization
questions.answer: Its syntax reads almost like plain English, lowering the barrier to entry for non-professional programmers

questions.question: What makes Python especially suited to the exploratory, trial-and-error nature of data analysis?
options: It is an interpreted language, so code runs line by line and results can be seen immediately
It is a purely compiled language
It requires the entire program to run before any output appears
It cannot be used inside a notebook environment
questions.answer: It is an interpreted language, so code runs line by line and results can be seen immediately

questions.question: What is Anaconda?
options: A Python distribution pre-packaged with major Data Science libraries plus the conda package/environment manager
A web browser used to run Python scripts
A cloud database service for storing datasets
A type of neural network architecture
questions.answer: A Python distribution pre-packaged with major Data Science libraries plus the conda package/environment manager

questions.question: What is a Jupyter Notebook?
options: An interactive coding environment where code runs in small, independently re-runnable blocks called cells
A command-line-only Python interpreter with no visual output
A spreadsheet application unrelated to Python
A version control system for tracking code changes
questions.answer: An interactive coding environment where code runs in small, independently re-runnable blocks called cells

questions.question: Which library is built around a fast data structure called an array (ndarray) for numerical computing?
options: NumPy
Pandas
Matplotlib
Scikit-learn

questions.question: Why are NumPy arrays generally faster than plain Python lists for large-scale numerical computation?
options: NumPy performs operations on an entire array at once using pre-compiled C code (vectorization), instead of a Python loop element by element
NumPy arrays can only ever store a single number at a time
Python lists always store their elements contiguously in one packed block
NumPy cannot perform any mathematical operations on arrays
questions.answer: NumPy performs operations on an entire array at once using pre-compiled C code (vectorization), instead of a Python loop element by element

questions.question: Which library's core structure is the DataFrame, used for working with structured, table-like data?
options: Pandas
NumPy
TensorFlow
PyTorch

questions.question: A Pandas DataFrame is best described as:
options: A two-dimensional, size-mutable, tabular data structure with labeled rows and columns
A single labeled column of data only
An unordered collection that automatically removes duplicate values
A fixed collection of items that can never be modified
questions.answer: A two-dimensional, size-mutable, tabular data structure with labeled rows and columns

questions.question: Which library is primarily used to create visual representations of data, such as line graphs, bar charts, scatter plots, and histograms?
options: Matplotlib
NumPy
Scikit-learn
TensorFlow

questions.question: Which library provides ready-to-use implementations of traditional ML algorithms (regression, classification, clustering) plus tools for evaluating performance?
options: Scikit-learn
TensorFlow
Keras
PyTorch

questions.question: Which library is described as a beginner-friendly interface sitting on top of TensorFlow, for defining and training neural networks with simple, readable commands?
options: Keras
PyTorch
NumPy
Pandas

questions.question: PyTorch is best described as:
options: A major deep learning framework widely used in research for its flexibility
A tool exclusively for reading and writing spreadsheet files
A database query language
A tool used only for cleaning missing values
questions.answer: A major deep learning framework widely used in research for its flexibility

questions.question: A plain Python list is generally more memory-efficient than a NumPy array for storing and computing on large amounts of numerical data.
options: True
False

questions.question: NumPy underlies many other Data Science and ML libraries, including Pandas, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and PyTorch.
options: True
False

questions.question: A function's parameters (or arguments) are the named inputs it accepts, and its return value is the output it produces.
options: True
False

questions.question: Anaconda's conda package manager keeps separate sets of packages per project (environments), so one project's requirements never conflict with another's.
options: True
False

questions.question: Which of the following are reasons libraries matter in Data Science?
options: They save time because common operations are already written and optimized
They are tested extensively by large developer communities, reducing errors
They always run slower than writing the exact same code manually in pure Python
They can improve performance since many are built on faster languages like C
answer: They save time because common operations are already written and optimized
They are tested extensively by large developer communities, reducing errors
They can improve performance since many are built on faster languages like C

questions.question: Which of the following are true about user-defined functions in Python?
options: A function is a named, reusable block of code that performs one specific, well-defined task
Parameters go in as input, and a return value comes out as output
A function must always modify a variable outside of itself to be useful
Default parameter values let one function body handle both a simple case and a customized case
answer: A function is a named, reusable block of code that performs one specific, well-defined task
Parameters go in as input, and a return value comes out as output
Default parameter values let one function body handle both a simple case and a customized case

questions.question: Which of the following are reasons dictionaries matter for data handling in Data Science?
options: A single row of a tabular dataset can be thought of as a dictionary of column-name keys to values
Dictionaries provide an efficient way to map values from one set to another, such as encoding categorical variables
Dictionaries underlie JSON, the standard format for exchanging structured data
Dictionaries can only ever store one single value in total, never key-value pairs
answer: A single row of a tabular dataset can be thought of as a dictionary of column-name keys to values
Dictionaries provide an efficient way to map values from one set to another, such as encoding categorical variables
Dictionaries underlie JSON, the standard format for exchanging structured data

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Jupyter Notebooks?
options: Code runs in small, independently re-runnable blocks called cells
Results such as tables and charts appear immediately below the cell that produced them
Code, explanatory text, and visuals cannot exist together in the same document
Only the changed part of an analysis needs to be re-run, not the entire program
answer: Code runs in small, independently re-runnable blocks called cells
Results such as tables and charts appear immediately below the cell that produced them
Only the changed part of an analysis needs to be re-run, not the entire program
